title: Record Controlled Folder Access state and test a scan of a CFA-protected folder
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: Derived criterion 1: the Controlled Folder Access state (Get-MpPreference EnableControlledFolderAccess) is recorded where the scan's last-access results are recorded, next to the fsutil disablelastaccess state, as SL-056's design asked (docs/design/SL-056-probe-every-file.md:107-108): missing

Derived criterion 2: a scan of a CFA-protected folder (Documents/Desktop/Pictures, or a folder added to CFA's protected list) is run with CFA on, and the outcome is recorded: whether the FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES listing open and the LastAccessTime=-1 set are blocked, and so whether the folder is still listed in full and counted as kept or fell back to a plain open: missing
Derived criterion 3: whether such a scan raises a CFA block or audit event, or a user-visible CFA notification, is recorded: missing

Recorder script against doc recipe: the proposal shipped tests/window/CfaScan.ps1 (-Prepare/-Observe/-Cleanup, JSONL, canary build, CFA-off rehearsal under both shells) so the person runs rehearsed code. The composition ships pasteable steps in the design note instead, trading rehearsal for less review surface and no AppArgumentTests exposure.

Helper placement: the proposal put the read beside the Fsutil helper inside HeldOpenTreeTests.cs. The composition gives it its own DefenderState.cs so its never-throw and counting shapes can be unit-tested.
Where the lists are counted: the proposal used Measure-Object in PowerShell. The composition emits raw JSON and counts in C#.

Positive control in the person recipe: an unsigned csc canary (chosen) against pointing the exe's own --report into R, which would use the same image but whose behaviour when the write is refused is unknown.
Rule scope: the Defender-settings rule covers tests/** only. eng/** and src/** could be added as separate entries if a later reviewer judges them likely places for such a call.
tests/window/CfaScan.ps1, its canary build and its CFA-off rehearsal log: rejected by the design. The pasteable recipe is in the design note and its ordinary-window blocks were run once as written.
An xUnit Fact that scans with CFA on, plus its Trait, filter clause and OptInTraitTests pin: rejected by the design.

Criteria 2 and 3 themselves, and Q-101: they need an administrator and a person at the desktop, and the Sandbox cannot run Defender. They are filed as the person's run; none of the CFA=on steps (the W-admin steps, the refused canary, the 1123/1124 message shapes, the notification) was run.
O-020 / M4, using C:\Users\Public\Documents as the primary fixture: waived, carried to SC-275.
O-021 / M5, a case-insensitive Defender-settings rule that also covers eng/**: waived, carried to SC-276. The rule appended by the engine is unchanged.

O-022 / M6, the PSModulePath strip and the 'case 2 is non-material' wording: waived, carried to SC-277. The strip is built as designed. The runner follows VolumeUsageTests.GetVolumeUsed (async reads, timeout, tree kill), and the class comment says so.
O-023 / M7, exposing the child's PID so the timeout Fact checks it is gone: waived, carried to SC-278. The Fact checks the returned text and elapsed time under a 30 s sleeper.
O-024 / M8, listing the allowed apps by name before and after the session and voiding on an existing match: waived, carried to SC-279. Step 1 does list both lists by name, as M1's fix asks.
The 'once per test process, in parallel' case (C-013) is not tested: the design judged it performance only. The static Lazy gives it.

Run the recipe in docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md as an administrator at the desktop (criteria 2 and 3). Fill the results table and read it with the key. That is the evidence for Q-101.

If a result is 'blocked, fell back' or shows a notification caused by the scan, decide the behaviour. Options: skip the keep-last-access open in CFA-protected folders (a KnownWorkarounds entry: one checkbox, on by default, with the in-app notice) or reopen Q-159.
Exercise TryOpenKeepingLastAccess when the write-attributes open succeeds but SetFileInformationByHandle(FileBasicInfo) fails. It needs a seam in Core's open path and was not exercised by spike #109.
Repeat the CFA run on Windows 10 and on a Defender platform later than 4.18.26080.4 (Q-205, Q-224).
The five waived minors are on the backlog as SC-275 to SC-279 (Public\Documents fixture, case-insensitive rule over eng/**, spawn-idiom wording, PID-gone check, allowed apps before and after).

Not measured: whether ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders is replaced by the 'N/A:' placeholder for a non-administrator once it is non-empty (it reads as an empty list on this PC). Describe handles both. The elevated step 1 listing in the recipe will show it.

deviation: Describe's contract expected 'allowed apps=1' on this PC. The measured value is the non-admin placeholder, so the contract's expected reading was wrong (review M1, accepted). The line now reads 'allowed apps=hidden from non-administrators', and the design note records the corrected reading.

deviation: The recipe uses three fixtures (R-off, R-audit, R-on), not the design's single R. The accepted M3 asks for a 48 h back-dated witness 'before every run, before arming'. One fixture cannot be back-dated again inside a protected folder without a write that CFA might itself refuse, so each run gets its own fixture, back-dated before arming. The control is back-dated and listed after each scan.

deviation: Describe has a sixth parameter, timeoutSeconds (default 20), so the 'timed out after N s' reason can be asserted for the 1 s timeout Fact. The runner is split into Run (returns the child's result) and Read, so tests can also run a custom script through the same environment preparation.

deviation: Two Facts were added that the design did not list, to discharge O-001 and O-002 without asserting a machine's setting: one compares the line with an independent fresh read and the other pins the line's place after the fsutil line in HeldOpenTreeTests.cs by reading that source file. The PSModulePath Fact checks what the child reports as its own path, not that the parent had a pwsh 7 path.
deviation: No outside defect is worked around, so no KnownWorkarounds entry or setting was added. The 'N/A:' placeholder is Defender's documented behaviour for a non-administrator, not a bug.

drift: The timeout Fact runs a 30 s sleeper where the design said a 5 s one. This appears only in the O-011 claim, not under deviations. It is a strengthening: a 1 s return now proves the kill rather than a short sleep.

drift: Run() waits up to 5 s more for the stdout and stderr pipes after the child exits (DefenderState.cs:89-90). If they do not close, the result is reported as 'timed out after 20 s' although the child exited, and the worst-case read is about 25 s, not the designed 20 s. Not declared; harmless.

drift: The design listed two real-runner Facts. The build has five: timeout, missing exe, a real non-zero exit, PSModulePath, and the fresh-read agreement. Two are declared; the real non-zero-exit Fact (ANonZeroExitIsNotReadWithTheFirstStderrLineFromARealChild) is not.
drift: ReadOnce wraps Read in a catch-all so the Lazy can never cache an exception. The design does not mention it, but it is consistent with the never-throw contract.

not reached: A scan of a CFA-protected folder with CFA in AuditMode or Enabled. Whether the FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY|FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES keep-open and the LastAccessTime=-1 set are refused, whether the folder is still listed in full, and whether it is counted as kept or fell back (derived criterion 2, Q-101). It needs an administrator to arm CFA, and the Sandbox cannot run Defender.
not reached: Whether such a scan raises a 1123/1124 event or a visible Windows Security notification (derived criterion 3). Only a person at the desktop can see a toast.

not reached: Which image CFA judges (the unsigned published exe), whether a custom protected folder is treated like Documents, and whether Tamper Protection (on, on this PC) refuses Set-MpPreference for CFA (O-014, O-015, O-016).

not reached: HeldOpenTreeTests.Record() printing the 'not read' line beside fsutil on a Windows without Defender. In the Sandbox the HeldOpenTree fixture refuses SYSTEM's temp folder (pre-existing TempTree rule), so only DefenderStateRecordTests' reads of the same Lazy line were seen there.

not reached: PCs where Defender runs in Passive, SxS Passive or EDR Block mode, an older platform, or a third-party antivirus. The fresh-read agreement Fact may go red there (O-025, waived to SC-282); not measured.
not reached: Whether ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders becomes the 'N/A:' placeholder for a non-administrator once it is non-empty. It is empty on this PC.
not reached: The branch where the write-attributes open succeeds but SetFileInformationByHandle(FileBasicInfo) fails. Neither spike #109 nor this slice exercises it.
not reached: Windows 10, and Defender platforms other than 4.18.26080.4 (Q-205, Q-224).

critique missed: The design imported three administrator-gated must-verify preconditions (published exe is the image CFA judges, a custom folder is judged like Documents, the person can arm CFA) as validate-slice obligations. The critique did not ask of each must-verify invariant whether any unattended stage can arm it. None can: the Sandbox has no Defender and arming needs an administrator. The rule is already recorded as lesson #398 and CC-006. Cost: validate-slice #1 halted on O-014..O-016 until they were waived to SC-287..SC-289.

critique missed: The design's 'a missing property prints ?' case rested on recalled ConvertTo-Json behaviour, listed as 'recalled' in outside_claims. The real 5.1 child builds a [pscustomobject] with every key and a missing cmdlet property serialises as null, never as an absent key. A one-line powershell.exe measurement settles it. The critique measured the allowed-apps placeholder but not this.

critique missed: The critique did not check the design's missing-exe Fact against the existing temp-route Fitness rules (the SL-096 SystemRootTempRoute patterns over tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests). The first build used Path.GetTempPath() for the non-existent path and broke the rule. The fix was a name under AppContext.BaseDirectory.

code-review missed: TheChildPowerShellStartsWithItsOwnModulePath asserts no child PSModulePath entry matches (?i)(?<![a-z])PowerShell\\(7\\)?Modules. That also matches any foreign '...\PowerShell\Modules' entry, such as SQL Server tools in the machine value, so the default suite goes red where the strip works. The first review pass had just filed the identical failure class on the sibling Fact (m1) and did not audit the other machine-state Fact.

code-review missed: Describe and Read claim 'Total / never throws' (DefenderState.cs:58, :119). An escaped lone surrogate ('\ud800abc') makes GetString() throw InvalidOperationException, and a raw lone surrogate makes JsonDocument.Parse throw ArgumentException. Both escape `catch (JsonException)`. The first pass did not run adversarial strings against the totality claim.

still unknown: Does Tamper Protection (on, on this PC) refuse Set-MpPreference -EnableControlledFolderAccess even from an elevated shell? Validate read IsTamperProtected and found no CFA policy key, but never tried the cmdlet. The recipe's Windows Security UI fallback exists, and AuditMode has no UI switch (recalled).

still unknown: Does ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders become the 'N/A:' placeholder for a non-administrator once the list is non-empty? It reads as an empty list here. DefenderState.Describe handles both shapes, but only the recipe's elevated step 1 listing will show which one occurs.

still unknown: What does the 'Controlled Folder Access:' line look like in HeldOpenTreeTests.Record() on a Windows without Defender? In the Sandbox the HeldOpenTree fixture refuses SYSTEM's temp folder (TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot), so only DefenderStateRecordTests' reads of the same Lazy line were seen there. The line itself was seen there as 'not read (...0x800106ba)'.

still unknown: Does the default suite stay green on a PC where Defender runs in Passive, SxS Passive or EDR Block mode, or on an older platform where EnableControlledFolderAccess may be null? This is unmeasured. It is the failure mode behind SC-282 and SC-283.

went wrong: The survey reported 'allowed-apps list has 1 entry' from an unelevated read. That was the placeholder 'N/A: Must be an administrator to view exclusions', not a count. The design copied it into the Describe contract as the expected reading ('allowed apps=1'). It was caught by the first critique (M1) and confirmed in build by a 17-row corpus (9 placeholder rows red before the fix, 8 real rows green). The cost was a major finding, a rewritten contract and a new corpus file.

went wrong: The builder added two Facts the design never listed: TheLineAgreesWithAFreshReadOnThisPc and TheChildPowerShellStartsWithItsOwnModulePath. Both assert machine-dependent state, against the design's own 'nothing turns red'. They drew m1 and R2-m4. Both were waived (SC-282, SC-283), so the shipped default suite can go red on Defender in Passive, SxS Passive or EDR Block mode (the AMRunningMode=\S+ regex rejects those names) and on a PC with a foreign '...\PowerShell\Modules' entry in its machine or user PSModulePath.

went wrong: Describe's 'total, never throws' contract was false when it shipped (R2-m5, SC-284). A lone surrogate throws InvalidOperationException or ArgumentException past `catch (JsonException)`. The comments at DefenderState.cs:58 and :119 still claim totality. Only ReadOnce's catch-all keeps the production line safe.

went wrong: Validate halted once on O-014, O-015 and O-016, the three administrator-gated must-verify preconditions design-slice had routed to validate. Code review had already said (m3) that they belong with the person, and build documented that. The obligation rows stayed open until the loop waived them to SC-287..SC-289. That was an extra validate lap with no code change.

went wrong: The headline question (Q-101) is unanswered. Only the CFA-off blocks of the recipe were run, at Medium integrity. The first real execution is a person's single administrator session, and Q-235 and lesson #340 say a never-run recipe draws findings.

went wrong: Code review's first pass missed R2-m4 and R2-m5. Both surfaced only in the second round, when the reviewer explicitly tried to break the code, and R2-m4 was a sibling of the round-1 m1 defect it had just filed.
